correctness.rationale: For W=Der(F_q[t]/(t^5)) in char 5, a nilpotent derivation with nonunit coefficient has order≥2 (q^3 points), while the nonzero-unit nilpotent locus is conjugate to ∂ and has (q−1)q^3 points, total q^4. Nonzero centralizers stratify into 1-dimensional open (q−1)q^3, 2-dimensional abelian (q−1)(q^2+q), and 3-dimensional Heisenberg (q−1); all allowed companions are nilpotent. In Heisenberg, pairwise commutation means rank≤1 of a 2×r matrix, with count q^r((q+1)q^r−q). Conditioning on first entry leads to C_m−C_{m−1}=(q−1)((q+1)^2q^{2m−2}+(q^3−q)q^{m−1}); C_0=1 yields C_m=(q+1)q^{2m}+(q^3−q)q^m−q^3 for all m≥0. GF follows by formal geometric sums. This is finite-field point counting, not geometric component enumeration.
